newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Argentine stocks continued their downward correction Wednesday and could continue to ease gently in the next one or two sessions before steadying, dealers said.

"What we're seeing is a logical technical correction after a long string of gains, but the underlying trend remains very firm based on strong economic indicators," said Jose Napoli at brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.7 percent to 759.91, extending Wednesday's 0.5 percent fall. Before that it had climbed 6.3 percent in 11 consecutive sessions of gains.
"The MerVal should find pretty good support at 750 and switch back to gains," Napoli said.
The broad market index closed off 0.2 percent in the session, with winners trailing losers 19 to 42 and 20 issues closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to a moderate 24.9 million pesos from 20.8 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals rose to 97.2 million pesos from 94.6 million Tuesday.
"We were trading about 30 million when the market was rising. If volume recovers again prices will probably go right back up on short-covering," another dealer said.

The day's standout was Bansud bank, which rose 1.7 percent on momentum from two major bank mergers this month, dealers said. "Bansud has a long way to go before it catches up with heavyweights Banco Frances and Banco de Galicia in terms of their relative share value -- you could say it was lagging the sector and investors have now wisened up," Napoli said.

The only other MerVal riser was oil giant YPF, which gained 1.0 percent. Main-tier losses were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, oil company Astra and steelmaker Siderar, which fell 8.5 percent, 2.2 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
